question: An item marked at ₹5,000 is given at successive discounts of 10% and 5%. Find the final selling price.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Successive discounts can be applied directly using multiplying factors.

Final SP = MP × (100 − D₁) / 100 × (100 − D₂) / 100

Final SP = 5000 × (90 / 100) × (95 / 100)

Final SP = 50 × 9 × 9.5 = 4275

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4,275.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹5,000

Successive Discounts: a = 10%, b = 5%

**Formula Used:**

Effective Single Discount % = a + b − (a × b) / 100

Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount Amount

 
 MP = 5000
 
 
• 
 

 −10%

 
 4500
 
 
• 
 

 −5%

 
 SP = 4275
 
 

 

 Effective Discount = 14.5%

**Calculations:**

⇒ Effective Single Discount = 10 + 5 − (10 × 5) / 100

⇒ Effective Discount = 15 − 0.5 = 14.5%

⇒ Discount Value = 14.5% of 5000

⇒ Discount Value = (14.5 / 100) × 5000 = 725

⇒ Selling Price = 5000 − 725 = 4275

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4,275.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always given on the Marked Price (MP) of an article. The selling price is calculated as SP = MP − Discount.

Successive Discount Rule

When two consecutive discounts d₁% and d₂% are offered, the overall effective discount is calculated using the formula: d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂) / 100.

Direct CP to MP Relation

A common and highly useful relation to connect Cost Price (CP) and Marked Price (MP) is: MP × (100 − Discount%) = CP × (100 + Profit%).
